email.body1:
John, saw Exiger landed the 2026 Gartner Leader spot and a place on the $919M GSA BPA for supply chain risk.

Momentum like that in national security usually means more in-market agencies in play than reps can cover, and that is where good deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Exiger's national security targets off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
John, quick follow-up for Exiger.

With a major BPA and Gartner Leader status to sell behind, the number tends to climb faster than headcount can, and most sales orgs cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit it. The gap surfaces late, when saving the quarter is already a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your national security team needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
John, last bit of proof for Exiger.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Exiger's reply rate likely compares to other high-growth GovTech and risk firms. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
